text:
inc-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — elevated 5xx rate + tail latency observed in us-east-1a affecting inference-api. Trigger: sustained GRPC error spike and KV-cache miss rate. Link: https://ops.metrics/redwood/inference/us-east-1a

alex (oncall): ack, I'm on it. Pulling logs and checking routing.

sara (eng): thanks. I'm watching the routing policy. can we start cross-az failover to us-east-1b (gradual)?

alex (oncall): yes. initiating weighted reroute now. running: `redwoodctl route set --service inference-api --from us-east-1a --to us-east-1b --weight 0.25`

ops_lead: copy. also running quick health checks on node pool in us-east-1a — any evidence of EC2 host level degradation or SG/NIC errors?

jay (sre): seeing elevated kernel tx_skb drops on several hosts, plus NLB target health transitions. kv-cache regen events line up with severity window.

sara (eng): mitigation: lowering weight to 0.1 and enabling prefix-kvcache bypass for new requests to reduce cache churn. command: ```bash
redwoodctl config update --service inference-api --kvcache bypass=true --bypass-scope new
```

inc-bot: AUTOMATED MITIGATION ENGAGED — cross-az fallback policy applied, canary traffic to us-east-1b started (10% -> 25% configured). Monitor: https://ops.metrics/redwood/inference/fallbacks

alex (oncall): after reroute: 5xxs down ~65%, p95 still elevated (~800ms). some requests still seeing stream reset (econnreset).

jay (sre): attaching short log snippet: `grpc: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection error: desc = "transport: Error while dialing"` — looks like intermittent ENI resets on a subset of hosts.

ops_lead: starting a limited instance drain on affected ephemeral pool in us-east-1a to remove noisy hosts. will keep a slow drain to avoid extra kv-cache churn.

chris (pm): customer impact check — our SLI page shows ~12% of requests during spike exceeded 500ms, and 3 tenants reported errors via status page. drafting comms for affected customers.

alex (oncall): also kicked off `kubectl get pods -o wide -n inference | grep CrashLoop` and `aws ec2 describe-instance-status --filters Name=availability-zone,Values=us-east-1a` — no full host OOMs but NIC errors in instance status.

sara (eng): rolling a targeted patch to the network driver retry settings on the ephemeral pool (small change) to reduce connection resets; will deploy to 5 hosts first as canary.

mike (night): acked via DM, I'll take NOC monitoring and escalate if the 5xx rate rises after alex signs off. details/links please.

alex (oncall): handing off: current state — mitigated (5xx reduced, latency improving), drain+patch in progress, routing set to 25% us-east-1b. watchlist: p95, kv-cache miss rate, NLB 502s. playbook: https://confluence/redwood/incidents/az-network-failover-playbook. handing to @mike (night) in 10m.

ops_lead: customer impact summary for post-incident review: ~45 minutes total alert window, ~20m active mitigation, ~2 customers briefly impacted with errors, no data loss.

jay (sre): will collect host-level traces and ENI metrics for postmortem. tagging: netplane, kv-cache, nlb.

inc-bot: STATUS UPDATE — mitigation in progress, monitoring for recurrence. incident severity: SEV2 -> monitoring.

mike (night): ack, monitoring. leaving a note in the oncall log and will open a follow-up ticket to validate driver patch across the fleet tomorrow. :thumbsup:
